title: Addendum to GPT-5 system card: GPT-5-Codex
paper_type_zh: 前沿编码代理系统卡增补与数据披露账本
best_for_zh: 审计 Codex 家族 SWE 任务、代码审查反馈、评测 verifier 与版本披露差异的研究者
one_line: GPT-5-Codex discloses RL on real-world project building, feature and test work, debugging, refactoring, and code review plus synthetic malware and new prompt-injection safety data, but not the task records, preference or reward representation, trajectories, split, or reusable artifacts.
GPT-5-Codex 披露了面向真实项目构建、功能与测试、调试、重构和代码审查的 RL，以及继承的恶意软件安全数据和新 prompt-injection 数据；其价值是区分训练目标、人工/测试评测与部署防护，但 reward 表示、trajectory、split 和可复用 artifact 均未公开。
why: It is a useful coding-agent disclosure ledger because it names concrete training task families and separates code-review training, experienced-engineer evaluation, executable tests, safety data, traffic observations, and product sandboxing that could otherwise be conflated into an unsupported reward or dataset claim.
inclusion_reason: A frontier coding-agent report that discloses reinforcement learning on several real-world software-engineering task families, code-review specialization, inherited synthetic malware safety data, and new coding-environment prompt-injection data, while exposing human and executable evaluation contracts but withholding task records, rewards, splits, licenses, and item-level lineage.

title: Problem
问题
html:
OpenAI published the seven-page Addendum to GPT-5 system card: GPT-5-Codex on September 15, 2025. It describes GPT-5-Codex as a GPT-5 version optimized for agentic coding and explicitly states reinforcement learning on real-world coding tasks across varied environments (PDF p.1). The associated launch page expands the task taxonomy to building projects from scratch, adding features and tests, debugging, large-scale refactoring, and code review.

The concrete Atlas problem is not whether GPT-5-Codex can edit code, but what post-training records and feedback could produce those behaviors. A plausible disclosed episode contains a software-engineering prompt, repository or project context, environment state, commands or tool actions, file edits and diffs, test executions, and a terminal artifact or review comment. OpenAI names desired outcomes—human-like code and pull-request preferences, precise instruction following, code review, and iteratively running tests until passing—but does not disclose whether they are scalar rewards, preference pairs, executable predicates, judge outputs, or a mixed objective.

Safety training adds two other data families. The report inherits a codex-1 malware policy and synthetic pipeline producing prompts, code snippets, and environment configurations, then says new Instruction Hierarchy data were created for coding-environment prompt injection (PDF §§2.1.2–2.2.2, pp.3–4). Neither family is released with item schemas, counts, labels, generators, splits, or licenses.

This belongs in frontier_reports_data_disclosure_ledger because it exposes task-family and behavior-level deltas while leaving the record ledger closed. It does not release an SWE dataset, agent trajectories, reward code, model weights, or replay environments. The current Deployment Safety Hub marks the model as no longer in production; that lifecycle status does not change the 2025 source identity but prevents product claims from being treated as current-model guarantees.

OpenAI 于 2025 年 9 月 15 日发布七页 Addendum to GPT-5 system card: GPT-5-Codex。报告将 GPT-5-Codex 描述为针对 agentic coding 优化的 GPT-5 版本，并明确说明它在多种环境的真实编码任务上接受 reinforcement learning（PDF 第 1 页）。配套发布页进一步列出任务 taxonomy：从零构建项目、添加功能与测试、调试、大规模重构和代码审查。

Atlas 的具体问题不是 GPT-5-Codex 能否编辑代码，而是什么后训练记录与反馈产生了这些行为。在披露边界内，一条 episode 可包含软件工程 prompt、代码仓库或项目上下文、环境 state、命令或 tool action、文件编辑与 diff、测试执行，以及终态 artifact 或 review comment。OpenAI 点名的目标包括类人代码与 pull-request preference、精确遵循指令、code review 和迭代运行测试直到通过，但没有披露它们属于 scalar reward、preference pair、executable predicate、judge output 还是混合 objective。

安全训练还加入两类数据。报告继承 codex-1 的恶意软件 policy 与合成流水线，后者生成 prompt、代码片段和环境配置；随后又说明为编码环境 prompt injection 创建了新的 Instruction Hierarchy 数据（PDF §§2.1.2–2.2.2，第 3–4 页）。两类数据都没有连同 item schema、数量、标签、generator、split 或 license 发布。

本报告属于 frontier_reports_data_disclosure_ledger，因为它披露了任务族与行为级增量，同时保持 record ledger 关闭。它没有发布 SWE 数据集、agent trajectory、reward 代码、模型权重或可 replay 环境。当前 Deployment Safety Hub 将该模型标记为不再生产使用；这一生命周期状态不改变 2025 年来源身份，但意味着产品陈述不能视为当前模型保证。

title: Core idea
核心思路
html:
The Card's one-sentence contribution is: GPT-5-Codex makes the GPT-5 coding specialization legible through real-world SWE task families, explicit RL, code-review specialization, inherited malware safety data, and new prompt-injection data, while leaving the actual reward and records unknown.

The main layer is agent training. The report says RL targets code resembling human style and PR preferences, instruction adherence, and iterative testing (PDF p.1). The launch page says code review navigates the codebase, reasons over dependencies, and runs code and tests. These statements identify desired behavior and an episode surface, not a complete feedback contract: PR preferences do not prove pairwise records or a preference model, and running tests does not prove that tests supply all or any training reward.

The second layer is evaluation. Recent commits from popular open-source repositories are reviewed by GPT-5-Codex, and experienced software engineers judge comments for correctness and importance. Other evaluations use all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, established-repository refactors, human mobile-web preferences, a policy-expert malware golden set, prompt-injection attacks, Production Benchmarks, StrongReject, CTFs, and Cyber Range. These human, test, policy, and environment predicates are evidence about evaluated behavior; none is established as the training verifier.

The third layer is deployment. Cloud and local sandboxes, default network denial, workspace restrictions, approvals, configurable allowlists or denylists, citations, terminal logs, screenshots, and test reports constrain or expose product behavior. They do not identify the RL environment, training examples, or reward.

The disclosure delta is version-specific. Base GPT-5 supplies broad source classes, router signals, and safe-completion context, not this Codex task ledger. The o3/o4-mini Codex addendum already disclosed real-world coding RL and the inherited malware pipeline, plus an unexpected-state false-completion reward that this GPT-5-Codex addendum does not repeat. GPT-5-Codex adds a clearer complex-task taxonomy and code-review training plus experienced-engineer review evaluation. GPT-5.1/5.2-Codex later disclose a conflicting-edit user model, preservation reward, compaction, and internal PR hidden tests; none may be backported here.

本 Card 的一句话贡献是：GPT-5-Codex 通过真实 SWE 任务族、明确 RL、code-review 专门训练、继承的恶意软件安全数据和新 prompt-injection 数据，使 GPT-5 的编码专门化更可读，但实际 reward 与记录仍为 unknown。

第一层是 agent training。报告称 RL 目标包括接近人类风格与 PR preference 的代码、指令遵循和迭代测试（PDF 第 1 页）；发布页说明 code review 会浏览代码库、分析依赖并运行代码与测试。这些陈述识别了目标行为和 episode surface，却不是完整 feedback contract：PR preference 不能证明存在 pairwise record 或 preference model，运行测试也不能证明测试构成全部或任一训练 reward。

第二层是 evaluation。GPT-5-Codex 审查热门开源仓库的近期 commit，经验丰富的软件工程师按正确性和重要性判断 review comment。其他评测使用全部 500 道 SWE-bench Verified 任务、成熟仓库的 refactor、人类 mobile-web preference、policy 专家 malware golden set、prompt-injection attack、Production Benchmarks、StrongReject、CTF 和 Cyber Range。这些 human、test、policy 与 environment predicate 是被评测行为的证据；没有一项被确立为训练 verifier。

第三层是 deployment。云端与本地 sandbox、默认禁止网络、workspace 限制、审批、可配置 allowlist/denylist、citation、terminal log、screenshot 和 test report 约束或暴露产品行为，却不能识别 RL 环境、训练样例或 reward。

披露增量具有版本边界。基础 GPT-5 提供宽泛来源类别、router signal 和 safe-completion 背景，不提供这份 Codex 任务台账。o3/o4-mini Codex addendum 已披露真实编码 RL 和继承的恶意软件流水线，以及本 addendum 未重复的 unexpected-state false-completion reward。GPT-5-Codex 新增更清楚的复杂任务 taxonomy、code-review 训练和经验工程师 review 评测。GPT-5.1/5.2-Codex 后续才披露 conflicting-edit user model、preservation reward、compaction 和内部 PR hidden tests；这些内容不能回填到本 Card。

title: Method
方法
html:
The method can be reconstructed only as a layered disclosure:

  1. Base and task sources. Start from an unspecified GPT-5 checkpoint and specialize it for agentic coding. Training tasks cover building projects, adding features and tests, debugging, large refactors, and code review in varied real-world environments. Repository IDs, revisions, prompt sources, task counts, rights, filters, and mixture weights are unknown.
  2. Agent interaction. The model navigates codebases, reasons over dependencies, edits files, runs commands and tests, and can produce project code, diffs, review comments, screenshots, citations, terminal logs, and test results. The report does not say which fields are retained in training trajectories, whether non-user-visible reasoning is stored, or how successful and failed episodes are selected.
  3. RL feedback. Reinforcement learning is explicit. Desired outcomes are human-like code and PR preferences, precise instruction following, code-review quality, and iterative test passing. The representation could involve human preferences, learned graders, executable tests, policy labels, or mixed rewards, but the report does not choose among them or give weights, calibration, reward scale, terminal predicates, or RL algorithm.
  4. Safety data. Reuse pre-existing safety data from the OpenAI hosted chat product and a codex-1 malware pipeline that generates prompts, code snippets, and environment configurations, including edge and adversarial cases; train refusal of high-risk requests and calibrated defensive or dual-use help (PDF §2.1.2, pp.3–4). Separately create new Instruction Hierarchy data for coding prompt injection and train the model to ignore attacks (§2.2.2, p.4). Counts, generators, labels, filters, overlap, and stage weights are undisclosed.
  5. Evaluation. Code-review evaluation pairs recent popular open-source commits with model comments and experienced-engineer correctness and importance judgments. SWE-bench Verified, refactor repositories, mobile-web preferences, malware golden-set cases, prompt-injection attacks, Production Benchmarks, StrongReject, CTF, and Cyber Range supply other evaluation predicates. Their tests and judges must remain outside the training reward unless an official source links them.
  6. Deployment. Codex CLI, IDE, cloud, and GitHub supply tool scaffolds and product controls. Cloud uses an isolated container with network disabled by default; local macOS uses Seatbelt and Linux uses seccomp plus landlock; users can approve broader access and configure project network policies (PDF §4, pp.6–7). These are deployment settings, not evidence of training substrate.

The general episode terminal predicate, rollout count, temperature, horizon, retries, optimizer, objective mix, compute, checkpoint selection, and stage allocation are unknown. A report that some test runs exceeded seven hours is evaluation or product observation, not a training horizon. CLI conversation compaction is also a product scaffold and must not be converted into compaction training evidence.

Reproduction would require task and repository manifests, pinned environments, action and observation schemas, review and preference records, successful and failed trajectories, test and grader versions, reward aggregation, global splits, decontamination, source rights, and item-to-checkpoint lineage. No such training package is released.

方法只能按分层披露重建：

  1. 基座与任务来源。 从一个未说明的 GPT-5 checkpoint 开始，面向 agentic coding 专门化。训练任务涵盖在多种真实环境中从零构建项目、添加功能与测试、调试、大型重构和代码审查。代码仓库 ID、revision、prompt 来源、任务数、权利、filter 和 mixture weight 均为 unknown。
  2. Agent 交互。 模型浏览代码库、分析依赖、编辑文件、运行命令和测试，并可产生项目代码、diff、review comment、screenshot、citation、terminal log 和 test result。报告没有说明哪些字段保留在训练 trajectory 中、是否存储 non-user-visible reasoning，也没有说明如何选择成功与失败 episode。
  3. RL 反馈。 Reinforcement learning 被明确披露；目标结果是类人代码与 PR preference、精确遵循指令、code-review quality 和迭代测试通过。其表示可能是人类 preference、learned grader、executable test、policy label 或混合 reward，但报告没有确定具体形式，也没有给出权重、校准、reward scale、terminal predicate 或 RL 算法。
  4. 安全数据。 复用来自 OpenAI 托管聊天产品的既有安全数据和 codex-1 恶意软件流水线；后者生成 prompt、代码片段和环境配置，并包含边界与对抗样例，用于训练拒绝高风险请求，以及校准的防御性或双重用途帮助（PDF §2.1.2，第 3–4 页）。另行创建新的 Instruction Hierarchy 编码 prompt-injection 数据，并训练模型忽略攻击（§2.2.2，第 4 页）。数量、generator、标签、filter、重叠和阶段权重均未披露。
  5. 评测。 Code-review evaluation 将热门开源仓库的近期 commit 与模型 comment 配对，由经验工程师判断正确性和重要性。SWE-bench Verified、refactor repository、mobile-web preference、malware golden-set case、prompt-injection attack、Production Benchmarks、StrongReject、CTF 和 Cyber Range 提供其他评测 predicate。除非官方来源明确连接，否则它们的测试与 judge 必须留在训练 reward 之外。
  6. 部署。 Codex CLI、IDE、cloud 和 GitHub 提供 tool scaffold 与产品控制。云端使用默认禁网的隔离 container；本地 macOS 使用 Seatbelt，Linux 使用 seccomp 加 landlock；用户可批准更广权限并配置项目网络策略（PDF §4，第 6–7 页）。这些是部署设置，不是训练 substrate 证据。

通用 episode terminal predicate、rollout 数、temperature、horizon、retry、optimizer、objective mix、compute、checkpoint selection 和 stage allocation 均为 unknown。部分测试运行超过七小时属于评测或产品观察，不能解释为训练 horizon。CLI conversation compaction 同样是产品 scaffold，不能转化为 compaction training 证据。

复现需要任务与代码仓库 manifest、固定环境、action/observation schema、review 与 preference record、成功和失败 trajectory、test/grader 版本、reward aggregation、全局 split、decontamination、来源权利以及 item-to-checkpoint lineage。此类训练包未被发布。

title: Evidence
证据
html:
The seven-page addendum provides model-specific safety numbers under named evaluation conditions. Table 3 on page 4 reports a malware golden-set refusal score of 1.00 for GPT-5-Codex versus 0.98 for codex-1; the set was curated by internal policy experts, but item count, uncertainty, rubric, and independence from training are not disclosed. Table 4 on page 4 reports successful ignoring of coding prompt injections at 0.98 for both GPT-5-Codex and codex-1; attacks include terminating the current task or planting an instruction for a later step. The paper does not disclose evaluation count or train/evaluation membership.

Production Benchmarks and StrongReject are separate safety evaluations. Table 1 on page 2 reports category-specific Production Benchmark scores; GPT-5-Codex ranges from 0.719 on harassment/threatening to 0.958 on sexual/exploitative and self-harm/intent, under conversations described as representative of production data. Table 2 on page 3 reports StrongReject robustness between 0.992 and 0.997 across four prompt groups. These numbers are author-reported safety scores, not evidence about the hidden SWE reward or corpus.

The launch page adds conditioned engineering evidence. SWE-bench Verified coverage changed from 477 runnable tasks at the GPT-5 launch to all 500 after an infrastructure fix. The refactor suite uses established Python, Go, and OCaml repositories; one Gitea example changes 232 files and 3,541 lines. During testing, some large tasks ran for more than seven hours while iterating over implementation and test failures. These are evaluation and product conditions, not training rollout counts or a universal terminal rule.

OpenAI employee-traffic telemetry reports that the bottom 10% of turns by model-generated tokens used 93.7% fewer tokens than GPT-5, while the top 10% spent about twice as long reasoning, editing, testing, and iterating; token counts include non-user-visible reasoning and final output. The sampling period, task distribution, raw traces, and statistical uncertainty are unavailable, so this is observational evidence rather than a controlled data or training claim.

For code review, the official launch page says evaluation uses recent commits from popular open-source repositories and experienced software engineers rate review comments for correctness and importance. It reports that GPT-5-Codex comments are less likely to be incorrect or unimportant, but gives no sample count, baseline values, repository and commit list, rubric, agreement, uncertainty, or raw labels. Hidden unit tests are not named for this review evaluation; those belong to later GPT-5.1/5.2-Codex internal PR evaluations.

All results above are direct OpenAI reports. The Card's interpretation is bounded: the data show that named evaluation surfaces exist under the stated conditions, but do not establish that their judges, tests, prompts, or metrics supplied the training reward or were independent of the task corpus.

七页 addendum 在明确评测条件下提供模型专属安全数字。第 4 页表 3 报告 malware golden-set refusal score：GPT-5-Codex 为 1.00，codex-1 为 0.98；该集合由内部 policy 专家整理，但 item 数、uncertainty、rubric 及其与训练的独立性均未披露。第 4 页表 4 报告 coding prompt injection 的成功忽略率：GPT-5-Codex 与 codex-1 均为 0.98；攻击包括终止当前任务或植入后续步骤指令。论文没有披露评测数量或训练/评测 membership。

Production Benchmarks 与 StrongReject 是独立安全评测。第 2 页表 1 报告分类别 Production Benchmark 分数；在被描述为代表 production data 的会话上，GPT-5-Codex 从 harassment/threatening 的 0.719 到 sexual/exploitative 与 self-harm/intent 的 0.958。第 3 页表 2 报告四类 prompt 上 StrongReject robustness 为 0.992–0.997。这些是作者报告的安全分数，不是隐藏 SWE reward 或语料的证据。

发布页补充带条件的工程证据。SWE-bench Verified 在 GPT-5 发布时只能运行 477 题，修复基础设施后覆盖全部 500 题。Refactor suite 使用成熟 Python、Go 和 OCaml 仓库；其中一个 Gitea 示例改动 232 个文件和 3,541 行代码。测试期间，部分大型任务运行超过七小时，并不断迭代实现和测试失败。这些是评测与产品条件，不是训练 rollout 数或通用终止规则。

OpenAI 员工流量 telemetry 报告：按模型生成 token 排序的 bottom 10% turn 比 GPT-5 少用 93.7% token，top 10% 则在 reasoning、editing、testing 和 iteration 上耗时约两倍；token 数包含 non-user-visible reasoning 和 final output。采样时段、任务分布、原始 trace 和统计 uncertainty 不可用，因此这是 observational evidence，而不是受控数据或训练主张。

对于 code review，官方发布页说明评测使用热门开源仓库的近期 commit，并由经验丰富的软件工程师按正确性和重要性评价 review comment。页面称 GPT-5-Codex comment 更少出现不正确或不重要情况，但没有给出样本数、baseline 数值、代码仓库与 commit 列表、rubric、agreement、uncertainty 或原始 label。该评测没有点名 hidden unit test；后者属于后续 GPT-5.1/5.2-Codex 内部 PR 评测。

以上结果均为 OpenAI 直接报告。本 Card 的解释保持边界：这些数据证明指定评测面在所述条件下存在，但不能证明其 judge、test、prompt 或 metric 提供了训练 reward，也不能证明它们独立于任务语料。

title: Novelty
新意
html:
The prior baseline is the May 2025 o3/o4-mini Codex addendum. It already disclosed RL on real-world coding tasks, human-style and PR-preference goals, a synthetic malware pipeline, coding prompt-injection data, and a concrete unexpected-state safety reward that penalized action-inconsistent completion claims. GPT-5-Codex changes the base family and improves disclosure of task specialization: full-project construction, features and tests, debugging, large refactors, and code review.

The most concrete new surface is code review. The report says the model is trained specifically to find critical flaws, compares PR intent with the diff, reasons over the codebase and dependencies, and runs code and tests. Its evaluation uses recent open-source commits and experienced engineers judging correctness and importance. This yields a human-judged (commit context, review comment, correctness/importance judgment) object, but the records, rubric, and training relationship remain unavailable.

Relative to base GPT-5, the delta is agentic coding specialization rather than a new broad-source claim: GPT-5's internet, partnership, and user or trainer source classes do not identify Codex tasks. Relative to GPT-5.1-Codex-Max and GPT-5.2-Codex, this earlier report is less specific about reward and environment interventions. It does not disclose a user model making conflicting edits, positive reinforcement for preserving those edits, native compaction training, or an internal PR benchmark graded by hidden unit tests.

RL, test execution, code review, human preferences, synthetic safety data, sandboxes, and long-running agents are not individually new. The novelty for the Atlas is disclosure granularity: task families and review evaluation become visible while the reward representation remains hidden. That gap makes the report useful for preventing a common inference error—turning observed test-passing behavior or evaluation graders into an unsupported training-verifier claim.

Before reuse, inspect task and repository manifests, revision pins, PR-intent and review-label schemas, preference representation, reward aggregation, test-to-reward mapping, failed trajectories, code-review false positives and negatives, global split, commit and benchmark overlap, licenses, and checkpoint lineage. Without them, this is a disclosure reference rather than an open construction recipe.

既有基线是 2025 年 5 月的 o3/o4-mini Codex addendum。它已经披露真实编码任务 RL、类人风格与 PR-preference 目标、合成恶意软件流水线、编码 prompt-injection 数据，以及一个具体的 unexpected-state 安全 reward，用于惩罚与 action 不一致的完成声明。GPT-5-Codex 更换了基础模型家族，并提高任务专门化披露：完整项目构建、功能与测试、调试、大型重构和代码审查。

最具体的新表面是 code review。报告称模型专门训练用于发现关键缺陷，会比较 PR intent 与 diff，分析整个代码库及依赖，并运行代码和测试。评测使用近期 open-source commit，由经验工程师判断 correctness 和 importance。由此形成一个人类判断的 (commit context, review comment, correctness/importance judgment) 对象，但记录、rubric 和训练关系均不可用。

相对基础 GPT-5，增量是 agentic coding 专门化，而不是新的宽泛来源主张：GPT-5 的互联网、合作伙伴和用户/训练者来源类别不能识别 Codex 任务。相对 GPT-5.1-Codex-Max 和 GPT-5.2-Codex，这份更早报告对 reward 和环境干预更不具体。它没有披露由 user model 制造 conflicting edit、保留这些 edit 获得正向强化、原生 compaction training，或由 hidden unit test 评分的内部 PR benchmark。

RL、测试执行、code review、人类 preference、合成安全数据、sandbox 和长时程 agent 单独看都不是新元素。它对 Atlas 的新意是披露粒度：任务族和 review evaluation 可见，而 reward 表示仍隐藏。这一缺口有助于防止常见错误推断——把观察到的测试通过行为或评测 grader 转换为没有证据的训练 verifier 主张。

复用前应检查任务与代码仓库 manifest、revision pin、PR-intent 和 review-label schema、preference representation、reward aggregation、test-to-reward mapping、失败 trajectory、code-review 假阳性/假阴性、全局 split、commit 与 benchmark overlap、license 和 checkpoint lineage。缺少这些材料时，本报告是披露参考，而非开放构造配方。

title: Limitations
局限
html:
• The real-world SWE ledger is task-family only. Repository identities and revisions, prompts, environment images, tool schemas, task counts, mixture weights, source rights, action trajectories, non-user-visible reasoning, successful and failed attempts, filters, and retention rules are unavailable.
  • “PR preferences” and human-like coding style name target behavior but do not establish pairwise records, annotator instructions, a preference model, scalar reward, optimization stage, weighting, or calibration. The main coding-agent feedback contract remains incomplete.
  • Iteratively running tests until passing is observed and desired behavior, not evidence that executable tests are the training reward. Tests can also miss semantic regressions, security flaws, and specification violations; a model can overfit a harness or make narrow changes that pass visible checks. These are curator-inferred reward-hacking risks.
  • Code-review evaluation has judgment risk. Experienced engineers score correctness and importance, but the repository and commit sample, rubric, labels per comment, inter-rater agreement, aggregation, false-positive and false-negative rates, and raw judgments are undisclosed. Recent public commits also create unresolved train/evaluation overlap.
  • The malware pipeline is inherited from codex-1 rather than a newly disclosed GPT-5-Codex construction. Generator versions, prompts, counts, labels, filters, golden-set independence, and failed examples are unknown. Its Table 3 result cannot attribute broader coding performance to this safety data.
  • New prompt-injection training data and the coding-focused evaluation lack a membership boundary, so robustness to unseen attacks cannot be distinguished from overlap. A 0.98 evaluation score also leaves unreported attack counts, uncertainty, severity mix, and failure examples.
  • SWE-bench coverage of all 500 tasks fixes an infrastructure gap, not benchmark decontamination. Refactor repositories and recent code-review commits lack cutoff dates, hashes, duplicate checks, solution-overlap analysis, or a global train/development/test manifest.
  • Employee-traffic token deciles, seven-hour tests, mobile-web preferences, safety benchmarks, CTFs, and Cyber Range are evaluation or observational surfaces. They conflate model, scaffold, task mix, budget, environment, and judge and cannot isolate the effect of training data.
  • Sandbox, network policy, approvals, screenshots, citations, terminal logs, and test reports are deployment controls or evidence surfaces. They cannot be used to infer the training container, reward, task correctness, or current product behavior after the model was retired from production.
  • The later Codex-family conflicting-edit user model, edit-preservation reward, native compaction training, internal PR hidden tests, and expanded Preparedness environments are not in this report. Backporting them would create false lineage.
  • No task corpus, preference or review records, safety data, model weights, reward implementation, evaluator code, replay environment, source-license ledger, decontamination report, or item-level checkpoint lineage is released. Reuse is therefore blocked beyond reading and audit reference.

• 真实 SWE 台账只到任务族层面。代码仓库身份与 revision、prompt、环境镜像、tool schema、任务数、mixture weight、来源权利、action trajectory、non-user-visible reasoning、成功与失败尝试、filter 和保留规则均不可用。
  • “PR preference”和类人编码风格点名目标行为，却不能确立 pairwise record、annotator instruction、preference model、scalar reward、优化阶段、权重或校准。主要 coding-agent feedback contract 仍不完整。
  • 迭代运行测试直到通过是观察到且期望的行为，不是 executable test 构成训练 reward 的证据。测试还可能漏掉语义回归、安全缺陷和 specification violation；模型也可能过拟合 harness 或进行只满足可见检查的窄修改。这些是 curator inference 的 reward-hacking 风险。
  • Code-review evaluation 存在判断风险。经验工程师评价 correctness 和 importance，但代码仓库与 commit 样本、rubric、每条 comment 的 label 数、inter-rater agreement、aggregation、假阳性/假阴性率及原始判断均未披露。近期公开 commit 还带来未解决的训练/评测 overlap。
  • 恶意软件流水线继承自 codex-1，而不是新披露的 GPT-5-Codex 构造。Generator 版本、prompt、数量、标签、filter、golden-set 独立性和失败样例均为 unknown。表 3 结果不能把更广泛编码表现归因于该安全数据。
  • 新 prompt-injection 训练数据与编码专用评测缺少 membership 边界，因此无法区分对未见攻击的 robustness 与 overlap。0.98 评测分数也没有附带攻击数量、uncertainty、严重性混合或失败样例。
  • SWE-bench 覆盖全部 500 题只修复了基础设施缺口，不是 benchmark decontamination。Refactor repository 与近期 code-review commit 缺少 cutoff date、hash、duplicate check、solution-overlap 分析或全局 train/development/test manifest。
  • 员工流量 token decile、七小时测试、mobile-web preference、安全 benchmark、CTF 和 Cyber Range 都是评测或 observational surface。它们混合 model、scaffold、task mix、budget、environment 与 judge，不能隔离训练数据效果。
  • Sandbox、network policy、approval、screenshot、citation、terminal log 和 test report 是部署控制或证据面，不能用于推断训练 container、reward、任务正确性，或模型退出生产后的当前产品行为。
  • 后续 Codex 家族的 conflicting-edit user model、edit-preservation reward、原生 compaction training、内部 PR hidden test 和扩展 Preparedness environment 均不在本报告中。回填这些内容会制造错误 lineage。
  • 没有任务语料、preference/review record、安全数据、模型权重、reward 实现、evaluator 代码、replay 环境、source-license ledger、decontamination report 或 item-level checkpoint lineage 被发布。因此，除阅读与审计参考外的复用均被阻断。

title: Usefulness
用途
html:
The safe reuse class is reading and audit reference only. The Card supports a versioned disclosure matrix for Codex reports: base checkpoint, SWE task families, repository and environment manifests, episode fields, review or preference labels, reward and terminal predicate, test integration, failed trajectories, safety data, split, license, and checkpoint lineage.

For agent-data design, the report suggests a target record containing task intent, pinned repository state, environment and tool versions, observations, commands, file edits, tests and results, final diff or artifact, review comments, human correctness and importance judgments, reward components, terminal status, and provenance. Both successful and failed episodes should be retained, along with whether the behavior came from training, evaluation, product telemetry, or deployment.

For code-review research, recreate the evaluation only with licensed and revision-pinned commits, a published rubric, multiple independent reviewers, agreement and adjudication rules, and explicit false-positive and false-negative analysis. Keep executable tests as a separate evidence channel from human importance judgments. Do not substitute the later internal OpenAI PR hidden-test setup for the recent-open-source-commit evaluation described here.

For reward research, test alternative interpretations of the hidden contract: human PR-style preferences, instruction-following judges, executable-test outcomes, review-quality labels, and mixed objectives. Budget-matched ablations should isolate whether gains come from task data, reward choice, long-horizon scaffold, or inference time. The current report supplies no implementation for any such baseline.

For deployment audit, use sandboxes, network defaults, approvals, citations, logs, screenshots, and test reports as controls and observability surfaces, not as proof of model correctness. Because the Safety Hub now marks GPT-5-Codex as no longer in production, any operational reuse must identify a current model and current product policy separately.

安全复用等级是 reading and audit reference only。本 Card 可用于建立 Codex 报告的版本化披露矩阵：base checkpoint、SWE task family、repository/environment manifest、episode field、review 或 preference label、reward 与 terminal predicate、test integration、失败 trajectory、安全数据、split、license 和 checkpoint lineage。

对于 agent-data 设计，报告提示的目标记录应包含 task intent、固定 repository state、环境与工具版本、observation、command、file edit、test 与 result、final diff 或 artifact、review comment、人类 correctness/importance judgment、reward component、terminal status 和 provenance。成功与失败 episode 都应保留，并标明行为来自 training、evaluation、product telemetry 还是 deployment。

对于 code-review 研究，只应使用有许可且 revision 固定的 commit 重建评测，同时发布 rubric、多个独立 reviewer、agreement 与 adjudication 规则，以及明确的假阳性和假阴性分析。Executable test 应与人类 importance judgment 保持为独立证据通道。不能用后续内部 OpenAI PR hidden-test 设置替代本报告中的近期 open-source-commit 评测。

对于 reward 研究，可分别测试隐藏 contract 的不同解释：人类 PR-style preference、instruction-following judge、executable-test outcome、review-quality label 和 mixed objective。预算匹配的 ablation 应隔离收益来自 task data、reward choice、long-horizon scaffold 还是 inference time。当前报告没有提供任一 baseline 的实现。

对于部署审计，应将 sandbox、network default、approval、citation、log、screenshot 和 test report 作为控制与可观察性表面，而不是模型正确性证明。由于 Safety Hub 目前将 GPT-5-Codex 标记为不再生产使用，任何 operational reuse 都必须另行识别当前模型与当前产品 policy。

title: Reading notes
阅读笔记
html:
• Read PDF page 1 and the launch page together: the addendum establishes real-world coding RL and desired behavior, while the launch page supplies the project-building, feature/test, debugging, refactor, and review task taxonomy.
  • Keep code-review training distinct from evaluation on recent open-source commits judged by engineers for correctness and importance; no hidden-test contract is disclosed for this evaluation.
  • Treat all tests, SWE-bench tasks, refactor tasks, mobile preferences, golden sets, prompt injections, traffic telemetry, CTFs, and Cyber Range results as evaluation or observation unless explicitly linked to training.
  • Compare disclosure deltas: GPT-5 gives broad source and router context; o3/o4-mini Codex gives the unexpected-state reward; GPT-5-Codex adds task and review specificity; GPT-5.1/5.2-Codex later add conflicting-edit preservation rewards and internal PR hidden tests.
  • Attach every number to its condition: Tables 3–4 are safety evaluations, 500 SWE-bench tasks follow an infrastructure fix, seven-hour runs are testing observations, and token-decile results are employee telemetry.
  • Before reuse, request task and commit manifests, trajectory records, preference and review labels, reward or test mapping, failed episodes, global split, decontamination, licenses, and checkpoint lineage.

• 将 PDF 第 1 页与发布页一起阅读：addendum 确立真实编码 RL 和目标行为，发布页补充项目构建、功能/测试、调试、重构与 review 任务 taxonomy。
  • 将 code-review 训练与近期 open-source commit 上由工程师判断 correctness 和 importance 的评测分开；本评测没有披露 hidden-test contract。
  • 除非明确连接到训练，否则所有 test、SWE-bench task、refactor task、mobile preference、golden set、prompt injection、traffic telemetry、CTF 和 Cyber Range 结果都按 evaluation 或 observation 处理。
  • 比较披露增量：GPT-5 给出宽泛来源与 router 背景；o3/o4-mini Codex 给出 unexpected-state reward；GPT-5-Codex 增加任务和 review 细节；GPT-5.1/5.2-Codex 后续才加入 conflicting-edit preservation reward 和内部 PR hidden test。
  • 让每个数字附着于条件：表 3–4 是安全评测，500 道 SWE-bench 任务来自基础设施修复，七小时运行是测试观察，token-decile 结果是员工 telemetry。
  • 复用前索取 task/commit manifest、trajectory record、preference/review label、reward/test mapping、失败 episode、全局 split、decontamination、license 和 checkpoint lineage。

value.html: Training is described at the task-family level: real-world software-engineering tasks in varied environments, including building projects from scratch, adding features and tests, debugging, large-scale refactoring, and code review. Safety training additionally uses inherited safety data from the OpenAI hosted chat product and codex-1 malware-policy data, a synthetic pipeline producing malware-relevant prompts, code snippets, and environment configurations, and newly created prompt-injection safety data for coding environments. Task and repository identities, counts, dates, mixture weights, rights, and item records are unknown. Evaluation-only sources include SWE-bench Verified, refactor tasks from established Python, Go, and OCaml repositories, recent commits from popular open-source repositories, mobile website preference tasks, a policy-expert malware golden set, coding prompt-injection attacks, Production Benchmarks, StrongReject, CTFs, and Cyber Range; these must not be relabeled as training data.

Training target serialization is unknown. Disclosed model outputs include project code, feature and test additions, bug fixes, large refactors, review comments, commands, file edits and diffs, safety refusals or defensive and contextual answers, screenshots, citations, terminal logs, and test results. Evaluation records may pair recent commits with review comments and engineer correctness or importance judgments, prompts with policy or golden-set outcomes, or coding tasks with tests and terminal outcomes; complete schemas and examples are not released.

GPT-5-Codex acts in coding environments during reinforcement learning and product or evaluation episodes, but the report does not identify rollout generators, retained trajectories, hidden-reasoning records, accepted and rejected attempts, or item-level lineage. Code-review evaluation outputs are produced by GPT-5-Codex and judged by experienced software engineers; product tasks may expose citations, terminal logs, diffs, screenshots, and test results. OpenAI employee-traffic telemetry counts non-user-visible reasoning plus final output, but raw traffic traces are not released or claimed as training data.

Training uses an unspecified variety of real-world coding environments; the synthetic malware pipeline also creates environment configurations, but repository snapshots, container images, tools, permissions, network state, observation schema, and replayability are unknown. Evaluation and product substrates include large established repositories, recent popular open-source commits, Codex CLI, IDE, cloud, and GitHub, test execution, browser and screenshot iteration, and long-running agent tasks. Cloud containers, Seatbelt, seccomp and landlock, network-denied defaults, workspace restrictions, and per-project network controls are deployment safeguards and cannot be assumed to match training environments.

Reinforcement learning is explicit, and desired behavior includes human-like code and pull-request preferences, precise instruction following, code review, and iteratively running tests until passing. The report does not disclose whether these are scalar rewards, preference pairs, separate graders, executable tests, or a mixed objective, nor their weights or calibration. Evaluation contracts are separate: experienced engineers judge review comments for correctness and importance; humans provide mobile-web preferences; internal policy experts curate a malware golden set; prompt-injection attacks test whether malicious instructions are ignored; safety benchmarks measure refusal and robustness; and coding tasks use tests and observed task completion. None is established as the complete training verifier.

The general RL episode termination rule is unknown. The report says the model iteratively runs tests until passing and describes test episodes exceeding seven hours, but does not establish a universal all-tests-pass terminal predicate or maximum horizon. Evaluation and product episodes can end with a completed implementation, refactor, review, safety response, ignored prompt injection, or reported test result.

GPT-5-Codex is described as a version of GPT-5 optimized for agentic coding. Architecture, parameter count, exact base and final checkpoints, inherited GPT-5 stages, and allocation between general and Codex-specific training are unknown.
unknown

A synthetic pipeline generates malware-relevant prompts, code snippets, and environment configurations. The model or program generating these records, generator prompts, seeds, decoding, human review, and versions are unknown. No generator is identified for real-world software-engineering tasks or prompt-injection safety records.

Training sampling and task mixture are unknown. Evaluation sampling includes all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks after an infrastructure fix, refactor-style tasks from established repositories, recent commits from popular open-source repositories for code review, and OpenAI employee-traffic top and bottom token-use deciles. Counts and selection rules for refactor, review, preference, golden-set, prompt-injection, and traffic evaluations are mostly undisclosed.

Training rollout counts are unknown. The launch page reports that some test runs lasted more than seven hours, but gives no number of episodes, horizon distribution, retries, branching, or group size.
unknown

The malware pipeline includes edge cases and adversarial examples and targets refusal of high-risk requests, defensive or contextual help, and calibrated dual-use handling. No admission rules, repository filters, solvability checks, policy-label process, task deduplication, rejection reasons, yields, or retained and failed-example policy are disclosed for the main coding or safety data.

Training budgets are unknown. At evaluation and product time, GPT-5-Codex dynamically varies effort with task complexity, has been observed working for more than seven hours on large tasks, and shows different token use across employee-traffic deciles. Codex CLI can compact conversation state, but this is a product scaffold disclosure rather than evidence of a GPT-5-Codex training curriculum or fixed model budget.

OpenAI explicitly reports reinforcement learning on real-world coding tasks in varied environments and additional safety training for malware and prompt injection. The RL algorithm, reward construction, preference representation, executable-test use, objective weights, optimizer, batch and rollout schedule, replay, KL treatment, compute, checkpoint selection, and stage accounting are unknown.

The report names real-world software-engineering task families, human-style and PR-preference goals, inherited malware safety data, synthetic malware scenarios, and new prompt-injection data, but gives no quantitative mixture. Base GPT-5 broad source classes are inherited context and do not identify the Codex task corpus. Source manifests, repositories, revisions, counts or tokens, dates, privacy and consent handling, and source-level rights are unknown.

No global training, development, and test split or membership ledger is disclosed. The malware golden set, coding prompt-injection suite, SWE-bench, refactor tasks, recent-commit code-review evaluation, mobile-web preference evaluation, Production Benchmarks, StrongReject, CTFs, and Cyber Range are described as evaluation objects, but their overlap with the real-world training tasks and safety data is not reported.

No repository-level, commit-level, benchmark, prompt-injection, or safety-data decontamination audit is disclosed. Running all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks fixes evaluation infrastructure coverage but does not establish train and test independence. Recent open-source commits and established-repository refactor tasks lack disclosed cutoff dates, hashes, or overlap checks.

items: The phrase PR preferences names a desired behavior but does not disclose pairwise preference records, a preference model, label protocol, reward function, or preference-learning stage.

Iteratively running tests until they pass is reported behavior, not proof that tests are the complete RL reward, that all tasks have executable tests, or that passing tests guarantees semantic correctness.

Real-world task families lack repository identities, revisions, environment images, task counts, source rights, retained trajectories, failed attempts, and a reproducible sampling or filtering recipe.
The synthetic malware pipeline is described as developed for codex-1; treating it as a newly constructed GPT-5-Codex release or attributing GPT-5-Codex gains to it would overstate the delta.
The new prompt-injection training data and coding-focused evaluation have no disclosed membership boundary, so training and evaluation overlap and robustness to unseen attacks cannot be audited.

Code-review evaluation uses recent open-source commits and experienced engineer judgments, but omits repository and commit lists, sample counts, rubric details, agreement, raw comments, false positives, false negatives, and train and evaluation overlap.

SWE-bench, refactor, preference, seven-hour task, employee-traffic, safety, CTF, and Cyber Range results are evaluation or observational evidence; they do not reveal the training corpus or isolate causal effects of RL data.

The current Deployment Safety Hub marks GPT-5-Codex as no longer in production; aliases and product behavior may have changed, so deployment claims require a date and should not be treated as current-model guarantees.

Cloud and local sandboxing, configurable network access, user approvals, citations, terminal logs, and test reports are product controls and evidence surfaces, not training examples or model-internal correctness guarantees.
The later GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 Codex conflicting-edit reward, internal OpenAI PR hidden tests, compaction training, and expanded Preparedness objects are absent here and must not be backported.
No open data, model weights, reward implementation, global decontamination audit, source-license ledger, or item-level checkpoint lineage is released.

Source-level rights are unknown.

Stage-level lineage connects GPT-5 to GPT-5-Codex, real-world software-engineering RL, additional human-style coding data, inherited and synthetic malware safety training, and newly created prompt-injection safety data, followed by human, executable, benchmark, traffic, and Preparedness evaluations plus deployment safeguards. Prompt-to-repository-to-environment-to-action and test trajectory-to-feedback-to-reward-to-checkpoint lineage, dataset versions, record IDs, and checkpoint hashes are unavailable.
